_note: Facts for the Flight Viewer (international) narration/captions. pairs = unordered ICAO pair -> true, number-light lines. airports = destination airport fact. superlatives = unordered pair -> {label,hook}; hook uses {from}/{to} city names. Longest/shortest/busiest data: AirAdvisor (Sept 2026), OAG (2024/2025). Re-check before relying on rankings.

EGLL-KJFK: London Heathrow and New York JFK is the busiest long haul international route, and the only one in the top ten that crosses an ocean.
Supersonic Concorde once covered it in about three and a half hours before retiring in 2003.
EGLL-KLAX: This route links the United Kingdom's biggest airport with the heart of the American entertainment industry.
EGLL-OMDB: This route connects Europe with Dubai, one of the world's great transfer hubs between Europe, Asia and Africa.
OMDB-YSSY: It is one of the key links between the Gulf and Australia, crossing the Indian Ocean on a very long flight.
EGLL-WSSS: It is a classic leg of the Kangaroo Route, the historic air link between Britain and Australia.
WSSS-YSSY: It links two of the busiest gateways in Asia Pacific, and Singapore is a major transfer point for Australia.
KLAX-YSSY: This trans Pacific route crosses the International Date Line, so the calendar date jumps during the flight.
KLAX-RJTT: This trans Pacific route links two giant Pacific coast economies, Southern California and Japan.
KJFK-RJTT: It connects two of the largest metropolitan areas on Earth, New York and Tokyo.
KJFK-OTHH: It links New York with Qatar's Gulf hub on a long flight across the Atlantic and Europe.
EGLL-OTHH: It links London with Doha, a major hub connecting Europe to Asia, Africa and Australia.
EGLL-VHHH: It is a classic Europe to Asia route, linking London with one of the world's great financial centers.
KJFK-LFPG: It links two of the world's most visited cities across the North Atlantic.
EDDF-KJFK: It connects Frankfurt, a major European financial center, with New York across the North Atlantic.
EDDF-KORD: It links Frankfurt with Chicago, one of the biggest hubs in the United States.
KJFK-OMAA: Abu Dhabi offers United States border preclearance, so travelers heading to America clear immigration before they fly.
KLAX-RKSI: It links Seoul with Los Angeles, home to one of the largest Korean communities outside Korea.
KSFO-RJTT: It links Silicon Valley's gateway with the heart of Tokyo across the North Pacific.
KJFK-LTFM: It links New York with Istanbul, a city that sits on two continents.
EGLL-LTFM: It links London with Istanbul, a city that sits on both Europe and Asia.
EHAM-KJFK: Amsterdam is home to KLM, founded in 1919 and the oldest airline still flying under its original name.
EHAM-KLAX: It links Amsterdam with Los Angeles, a long transatlantic and continental flight on the KLM network.
EGLL-VIDP: It links London with Delhi, one of the busiest air corridors between Europe and South Asia.
EGLL-FACT: It links London with Cape Town, one of the longest running air links between Britain and southern Africa.
LFPG-SBGR: It crosses the Atlantic between Paris and Sao Paulo, linking Europe with South America's largest city.
CYYZ-EGLL: It links Toronto with London, one of the busiest air links between Canada and Europe.
CYVR-RJTT: It links Vancouver, Canada's gateway to Asia, with Tokyo across the North Pacific.
KLAX-EHAM: It links Amsterdam with Los Angeles, connecting Europe to the American West Coast.
KJFK-WSSS: Singapore Airlines flies it non-stop in both directions, close to nineteen hours in the air.
KEWR-WSSS: It is the sister flight to Singapore Airlines' New York JFK service, and both rank at the very top of the world's longest flights.
EGLL-YPPH: Qantas links London and Perth non-stop, connecting Britain with the west coast of Australia.
KDFW-YMML: Qantas connects Texas with Melbourne non-stop, one of the longest routes in the world.
KJFK-NZAA: It links New Zealand's biggest city with New York across the Pacific and the Americas.
NZAA-OMDB: Emirates links Auckland with Dubai non-stop, among the longest flights in the world.
KLAX-WSSS: It links the American West Coast with Singapore across the Pacific on an ultra long haul flight.
OBBI-OEDF: The two cities are also joined by the King Fahd Causeway, a road bridge across the water.
OBBI-OTHH: Bahrain and Qatar are neighbors across the Persian Gulf, so the flight is a short hop of under an hour.
OMDB-OOMS: It links the United Arab Emirates and Oman on a short regional hop.
RCTP-VHHH: Hong Kong and Taipei is the busiest international air route in the world by seat capacity, according to OAG's 2025 ranking.
HECA-OEJN: Jeddah is the main gateway for pilgrims traveling to Mecca, which helps make this one of the busiest routes in the world.
WMKK-WSSS: Malaysia and Singapore are close neighbors, and this short hop ranks among the busiest international routes anywhere.
RJAA-RKSI: It links the Seoul area with Tokyo and was the second busiest international route in the world in 2024.
RJBB-RKSI: Osaka is one of Japan's most popular destinations for Korean travelers.
WIII-WSSS: Jakarta and Singapore link Indonesia's capital with one of Southeast Asia's biggest hubs.
OERK-OMDB: Dubai and Riyadh link two of the biggest business centers in the Gulf.
VHHH-VTBS: Bangkok and Hong Kong link two of Asia's biggest travel hubs.
RCTP-RJAA: Tokyo and Taipei are close partners in business and tourism.
OMDB-VABB: Dubai and Mumbai link the Gulf with one of India's biggest cities, home to a large Indian community in the United Arab Emirates.
OMDB-VIDP: Delhi and Dubai are among the busiest air links between India and the Gulf.
NZAA-YSSY: Sydney and Auckland is one of the busiest international routes in the Southern Hemisphere.
EGLL-EIDW: London and Dublin is one of the busiest international routes in Europe.
EGLL-EHAM: London and Amsterdam link two of Europe's biggest airport hubs.
RJTT-RKSS: Seoul Gimpo and Tokyo Haneda connect two city airports, a popular route for business travelers.
VTBS-WSSS: Singapore and Bangkok link two of Southeast Asia's busiest hubs.
VHHH-WSSS: Singapore and Hong Kong link two of Asia's biggest financial centers.
CYYZ-KJFK: Toronto and New York is one of the busiest air links between Canada and the United States.
KLAX-MMMX: Los Angeles and Mexico City link the United States with one of the largest cities in the Americas.
SAEZ-SBGR: Sao Paulo and Buenos Aires link two of South America's biggest cities.
SCEL-SPJC: Lima and Santiago link the capitals of Peru and Chile.
MPTO-SKBO: Bogota and Panama City connect South America to Copa Airlines' hub in Panama.
HAAB-HKJK: Nairobi and Addis Ababa link two of East Africa's main hubs, home to Kenya Airways and Ethiopian Airlines.
EDDF-EGLL: Frankfurt and London link two of Europe's biggest financial centers.
EGLL-LEMD: Madrid and London link Spain's capital with the United Kingdom.
LEBL-LFPG: Barcelona and Paris link two of Europe's most visited cities.
OMDB-OTHH: Doha and Dubai link two of the Gulf's biggest transfer hubs.
